findings.severity_note: the reuse dimension is scored 5 on this; consolidating onto the existing helper (lazily imported, as the file already lazily imports reckon/crew/picker) is cleanup, not a correctness repair, so it does not hold the node.
findings.text: _trim_log_to_bound duplicates reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:566 trim_file_ends / :610 trim_service_log, which already keep a file's newest whole lines under a byte limit; the addition neither extends nor wraps that owner, so one capability now has two implementations free to drift.

findings.severity_note: narrow: it needs two lanes' services appending to the shared log inside the read-to-replace window; the loss is one verdict line, never an admission decision.
findings.text: the trim reads the tail and then replaces the file with os.replace while running outside _admit_lock, so a verdict line appended by a concurrent admission service between the read and the replace is silently discarded, and two concurrent trims share the fixed .tmp name.

findings.severity_note: the same revision is named in the manifest's artifacts and test_logs lines; repair by naming fc3462af8 for the focused gate, leaving 388b92530 for the importer head arm and the negative control, which their logs do name.
findings.text: the measure paragraph names 388b92530 for the focused gate, but the paragraph's own opening sentence says each revision is the one named on its own log's first line and logs/focused-head.log line 1 names fc3462af8ae20865c955317ee18b198b34d6037e; the code is identical between those two revisions so the evidence stands, but the citation is contradicted by the artefact it cites.
